Here's a full breakdown of **PocketLauncher**:

---

## What It Is

A **retro gaming "console OS"** for Android — specifically Android handhelds like the Retroid Pocket G2. Instead of launching external emulator apps, it embeds everything under one unified roof:

```
Jetpack Compose UI → Native libretro Host (C++) → mGBA core → GB/GBC/GBA games
```

The UX is deliberately console-like: pure dark theme, amber accents, 100% D-pad/button operated, immersive fullscreen with no Android chrome visible.

---

## Architecture

It's a clean **MVVM + single-activity** structure:

- **[`MainActivity`](https://github.com/SHAD0WDEM0N/PocketLauncher/blob/master/app/src/main/java/com/example/pocketlauncher/MainActivity.kt)** — single Compose host, intercepts all raw `KeyEvent`s before Compose touches them, enforces immersive mode.
- **[`MainViewModel`](https://github.com/SHAD0WDEM0N/PocketLauncher/blob/master/app/src/main/java/com/example/pocketlauncher/MainViewModel.kt)** — `StateFlow`-based single source of truth; handles screen routing and D-pad navigation logic.
- **[`PocketInputMapper`](https://github.com/SHAD0WDEM0N/PocketLauncher/blob/master/app/src/main/java/com/example/pocketlauncher/input/PocketInputMapper.kt)** — translates raw Android keycodes to `PocketButton` enums; uses a layered device profile system for per-device overrides.
- **[`pocket_engine.cpp`](https://github.com/SHAD0WDEM0N/PocketLauncher/blob/master/app/src/main/cpp/pocket_engine.cpp)** — C++20 JNI stub; currently just proves the Kotlin → NDK bridge works; will become the libretro host in Phase 2.

---

## Current Status — Phase 0 ✅ (v0.2.0)

The foundation is done: theme system, full-screen UI, controller routing, JNI bridge verified, and a built-in **Input Diagnostic Screen** (`Settings → Input Test`) that shows live button state + an event log. You can install a working APK from the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/SHAD0WDEM0N/PocketLauncher/releases) page today.

---

## What's Next

The 6-phase roadmap goes: input abstraction → libretro C host → mGBA boot → ROM library scanner → save states → quick resume. The big milestone is **Phase 3**: the first actual GBA game booting inside the launcher without any app-switching.

The full summary (with architecture diagram, tech stack table, and roadmap) is in the artifact above.
